transcript:
[00:00] Alex Navarro: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. We also have Samir, our SE, and Jordan on the call. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya Rao: Good good, thanks. Excited to see the SDK stuff, we've skimmed the docs but want a quick hands-on.
[00:15] Alex Navarro: Great. Agenda - 4 quick intro, walkthrough of the Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth and env setup, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:24] Samir Patel: I can start with the Python quickstart - I'll share my screen. Note, if the screen shows the repo it's the redwood-sdk-quickstarts repo, sorry if the name's slightly different in my browser.
[00:33] [screen share begins]
[00:36] Samir Patel: Ok so in Python we have a tiny example - pip install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var, then:
[00:45] Samir Patel: from redwood import RedwoodClient
[00:49] Samir Patel: client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
[00:55] Samir Patel: resp = client.generate("Write a product description for a green sweater")
[01:02] Liam O'Neal: Is that blocking sync call? We have a bunch of worker processes so non-blocking would be better.
[01:08] Samir Patel: Good call - the SDK supports async; example: async with RedwoodClient(...): await client.generate_async(...). There's also streaming support for low latency token-by-token handling.
[01:18] Priya Rao: Any caveats for long sequences? We do chat transcripts up to 4k tokens sometimes.
[01:24] Samir Patel: Yes - model choice and sequence length impact latency and cost. We have curated profiles in the Console; you can pin model variants or use a lower-cost quantized variant for non-critical ops. For longer context we recommend models with optimized KV cache handling.
[01:36] [00:01:40] Jordan Lee: quick note, in console you can set per-route batching and cache policies so repeated system prompts can be cached.
[01:44] Evan Park: For auth, we currently use short-lived service principals in CI. How would Redwood fit?
[01:49] Alex Navarro: We support three common patterns - static API keys for dev/trial, short-lived service accounts for CI/CD using our token exchange, and enterprise SSO for human users (SAML/SCIM). For POC we'd usually issue a scoped API key tied to the trial account.
[02:02] Nora Diaz: Is there a way to rotate keys automatically? We need rotation for compliance.
[02:06] Samir Patel: Yes, keys can be rotated via the Console or API; we also support issuing ephemeral tokens via our service-account flow integrated with your secrets manager. Some customers wire K8s secrets or Vault to pull ephemeral tokens.
[02:17] Priya Rao: On the private deployment side, we might need VPC-only egress and KMS with our HSM. Is that supported?
[02:23] Alex Navarro: Absolutely - our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering or private link. For Dedicated we can also configure restricted egress. We'll do a security deep-dive.
[02:33] [02:33] Priya Rao: Great. Also SOC two - is Redwood SOC2 Type II?
[02:39] Alex Navarro: Yes, we are SOC2 Type II and have an ISO attestation coming. I'll share the security pack.
[02:45] Liam O'Neal: On performance, can you describe typical P50/P95 numbers? We need 100 qps with p95 under 200ms for small prompts.
[02:53] Samir Patel: We'll need to benchmark with your payloads. Hosted can do decent latencies, but Dedicated gives more predictable p95 at scale because of reserved GPU pools and batch control. For 100 QPS with low p95 we often recommend a small Dedicated pool or a hybrid routing policy. We'll run a benchmark and share the datapoints.
[03:10] [03:10] Priya Rao: Cool - show us the TypeScript quickstart?
[03:13] Samir Patel: Sure. npm install @redwood/cli or yarn add @redwood/sdk (note - repo naming varies in docs). Example: import {Redwood} from '@redwood/sdk'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const resp = await client.generate({ prompt: '...' });
[03:29] Priya Rao: Our frontend is Node + edge workers, any tips for using on edge?
[03:34] Jordan Lee: For edge, we recommend issuing ephemeral tokens from your backend and keep long-lived credentials off the edge. The SDK supports running in edge environments but watch for binary size; we have a thin HTTP client option.
[03:46] Evan Park: Quick q on telemetry and cost - can we get token-level cost breakdown per route?
[03:51] Alex Navarro: Yes - Console has per-route token breakdown and cost attribution. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization to lower unit costs and simulate cost impact.
[04:02] Nora Diaz: For the SDK, how do we set region preference? We need EU region for data residency.
[04:07] Samir Patel: Set region in the client config or env var REDWOOD_REGION=eu-west-1. For Private you can deploy in your region. We'll note EU residency for the POC.
[04:17] [04:17] Liam O'Neal: Any gotchas with CI secrets? We use GitHub Actions.
[04:21] Samir Patel: Use GitHub Environments or Actions secrets with restricted access. For service accounts you can mint short-lived tokens via our API and store them as ephemeral secrets.
[04:31] Priya Rao: Can you demo a tiny integration - like product blurb generation hooked into our API?
[04:36] Samir Patel: Yep - I'll run a small local script. (typing noises)
[04:43] Samir Patel: Running generate now... Output: "Green sweater with breathable merino - perfect for spring - machine washable, model wears medium." Apologies, transcribe is slightly off - redwood generate returned a few variants.
[04:55] Liam O'Neal: Looks fine. How about error handling? If model fails or times out what's the recommended pattern?
[05:00] Jordan Lee: We recommend a retry with exponential backoff for transient issues and fallbacks to a smaller model or cached response for degraded mode. Console has auto-fallback policies you can attach to routes.
[05:12] Priya Rao: For POC success criteria: we'll measure latency at 100 qps, quality on a set of 100 prompts, and unit cost. Does that align?
[05:18] Alex Navarro: Perfect, that's actionable. We'll run the benchmark against hosted first then a Dedicated pilot if needed.
[05:25] [05:25] Evan Park: Who should loop in our security folks? Priya and Nora will handle that.
[05:29] Alex Navarro: I'll put together the security pack and a calendar invite for the deep-dive.
[05:33] [05:33] Priya Rao: One more on SSO - we use Okta. How long to onboard?
[05:37] Samir Patel: SSO onboarding is typically 2-5 business days once we have metadata. SCIM provisioning takes a bit longer depending on your schema.
[05:44] [05:44] Jordan Lee: I'll send a checklist for Okta SAML/SCIM mapping.
[05:48] Liam O'Neal: About deployment - can the SDK be used in microservices where each service has its own identity?
[05:53] Samir Patel: Yep. We recommend service accounts per service with least privilege, attached to route-level policies so you can track cost and usage per service.
[06:02] [06:02] Alex Navarro: OK quick recap and next actions - Alex will send pricing, quickstarts and trial API key; Samir will run benchmarks; we'll schedule security deep-dive; Verdant to provide sample payloads and expected traffic patterns. Anything else?
[06:16] Priya Rao: That covers it. Thanks everyone.
[06:18] Alex Navarro: Thanks - we'll follow up via email with links.
[06:21] [call ends]

Notes/Artifacts shared: link: https://redwood.ai/quickstarts (shared in chat), link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (shared), repo: github.com/redwood/rdw-sdk-quickstarts (mentioned).
